This means if a queen is at $(r, c)$, no other queen can be at $(r-1, c-1), (r-1, c), (r-1, c+1), (r, c-1), (r, c+1), (r+1, c-1), (r+1, c), (r+1, c+1)$. Wait, the rule says "Queens may not touch, including diagonally." This is the standard "no touching" constraint often found in puzzles like this. It implies that for any two queens at $(r_1, c_1)$ and $(r_2, c_2)$, $|r_1 - r_2| \le 1$ implies $|c_1 - c_2| > 1$. Actually, let's re-read carefully: "Queens may not touch, including diagonally. Thus queens in consecutive rows cannot occupy columns differing by 1." This confirms the standard non-attacking constraint for adjacent rows is stricter than just diagonal attacks. It means $|c_1 - c_2| \ge 2$ if $|r_1 - r_2| = 1$. And obviously $|c_1 - c_2| \ge 1$ if $|r_1 - r_2| = 0$ (which is impossible since one per row). So, essentially, no two queens can be adjacent horizontally, vertically, or diagonally. This is the "no-touching" constraint.
